A page's `live()` streams now pause when you leave the page and resume when you come back, with no change to the 42 callers. It's committed on `worktree/jsonl-unsubscribe` (`1359b25e0`, `de7d9b089`), not merged.

**Pause instead of drop.** Dropping on leave would have broken `/framework/ai/`. The page is cached and starts its `page.jsonl` and `index.jsonl` streams once at load, so nothing would restart them on return. A paused stream releases the server subscription and re-subscribes from its saved offset, so only the lines missed in between arrive.

**How it works.** `core/Page/Page.class.js` sets `$page` and emits `left` and `entered` on itself. `live.js` in `ext/JSONL` hooks those two events, so core imports nothing from ext.

**Headless proof** on the worktree server, going from `/framework/ai/` to `/framework/core/` to `/framework/ext/JSONL/` and back:
- **Leaving:** the page's subscriptions were released with `unsubscribe` frames, and subscribe and unsubscribe frames were counted on the socket.
- **Returning:** the streams re-subscribed.
- **Streaming check:** a line I appended while away did not arrive; one appended after returning did.
- **Server side:** I counted the frames the browser sent, not the subscriptions `Tail.js` holds.

**Left open.** Streams started with no page active are never paused. In the probe those were 8 embedded `ai/tests` previews and `dev/mobile`. A `live()` call made after an `await` is credited to whichever page is current by then.

I added a bullet to `ext/JSONL/readme.md`. The readme had no "One socket" bullet, so it's a new one. I rewrote the "Leaving a stream" section in `doc/live.md`. The probe is saved as `doc/probe-unsubscribe.mjs`. The task log is landed in `session.jsonl`.

The save rule is written and tested, and it's committed in the worktree as `9f7d6192f` (not merged). The one part that doesn't work is `item.set("prop", anotherItem)`, which only stores a snapshot of the item.

- **Built and tested:**
  - An item added to a parent's list logs its deltas to the parent's store, nested under the child's id. Reloading the parent replays the child.
  - An item with its own file is skipped by the parent's store. `Task.open_ref` uses this.
- **Not built:**
  - `item.set("prop", anotherItem)` doesn't adopt the child, so its later changes are never logged. On replay it comes back as a plain object, not an item. The fix needs `Store.hops()` to find children held in a property, which is more than one method. I wrote the plan in `core/Item/doc/next.md` instead, and the tests record the gap.
  - Dynamic upgrade (an item moving itself from the parent's store to its own file) is only a noted idea.
- **One tail:** items, pages and tasks all tail through `ext/JSONL/live.js` `stream()`. The board logs use the `JSONL` class, which calls the same `stream()` directly rather than going through `Item`. So it's one engine with two entry points.
- **Tests:** `core/Item/Item.test.mjs` now passes with 15 assertions, and the Property, Session, Task and Project tests pass. `core/Task/TasksPage.test.mjs` needs a browser and timed out here. I didn't touch `core/Task/`.

The rule with ✅/⬜ marks and the "testing system is a need, not now (2026-10-20)" line are in `core/Item/readme.md`. The file:line findings are in `core/Item/doc/architecture.md`, under "Items save through their parent". I also logged the result and the finish line in the task's `session.jsonl`.

I made all three pool fixes in `Servex/Pool.js`. They're committed in the worktree (`3cb800106`) but not merged, and Servex is not restarted.

- **Unknown holder:** an explicit hold by a holder the registry has no row for is released once the slot is 12 hours old.
